newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies O.J. Simpson new trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies O.J. Simpson new trial.

text.p: The judge in O.J. Simpson's civil case on Monday denied him a new trial and upheld a multimillion-dollar damage award against the former football star for the deaths of his ex-wife and her friend.

Simpson was found liable by a civil court jury in February for the June 1994 stabbing deaths of his former wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman. He was acquitted of murder in criminal court in October 1995.

Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki, who presided over the civil trial, said in upholding the damages of $33.5 million: "The amount of the award in this case may be considered insufficient rather than expansive when compared to life in prison or death." He was apparently referring to Simpson's possible fate if he had been found guilty of murder in the criminal case.

Fujisaki, who had previously ruled that the families of the victims could attach Simpson's future earnings in order to collect the damages, said: "It would be unconscionable for the defendant in this case to profit from his actions ... The reprehensibility of this defendant is most grievous."

Echoing his sentiments, Fred Goldman, the father of Ronald Goldman, told reporters after the ruling: "This (Simpson) is a man who belongs in jail, sitting on death row. There is no amount of money that can be equitable to what he did."

Simpson's lawyers had argued that the judge made several reversible errors in his handling of the civil trial and they also brought up the possibility of jury misconduct and claimed the panel was racially biased.

In particular, defence attorney Daniel Leonard argued in his written motion, Fujisaki had denied the defence permission to put former detective Mark Fuhrman on the witness stand and had allowed the introduction of polygraph test results, which is illegal under California state law.
Fuhrman testified in the criminal trial that he found a bloody glove on Simpson's estate that matched one found at the murder scene outside Nicole Brown Simpson's condominium.

Simpson's criminal defence claimed Fuhrman planted the glove to frame Simpson and the former detective later admitted to lying on the witness when he testified he had never used the word "nigger" in the past 10 years.

The results of the private polygraph test, which indicated Simpson was lying when he said he did not kill his ex-wife and Goldman, were introduced by lawyers for the plaintiffs, leading Simpson's lawyers to demand a retrial. The judge refused.

Simpson's lawyers also claimed the civil damages were arrived at by the jury "by chance" with panellists writing down numbers, putting them in a hat and then averaging them out. But Fujisaki said this argument was based on hearsay from what jurors told reporters after the trial and was not admissible.

While the jury in the criminal case was made up mostly of blacks, there was only one black juror on the civil case panel. Leonard argued the civil jury was racially prejudiced against his client, who is black. Both victims were white.
But Fujisaki said he had already dealt with Leonard's points in his rulings during the trial and stood by them.

Fred Goldman, whose tireless pursuit of Simpson following his acquittal in criminal court led to the civil court case, said: "We are pleased that the judge recognised the severity of these heinous acts. There is no amount of money that can equate to the violent acts he committed."

The $8.5 million in compensatory damages and $25 million in punitive damages will be shared by Goldman; the two young children, Sydney and Justin, Simpson had with Nicole Brown Simplson; and Sharon Rufo, Ronald Goldman's natural mother.
